# forge Command Reference

Every `nmt-forge` subcommand, generated directly from the CLI parser so this
page cannot drift from the tool. For the *why* behind each guard and for
driving forge from an agent, see
[Training with nmt-forge](/docs/agents/training); for the plain-words story, see
[Your first translator](/docs/your-first-translator).

**The global flag:** `--workspace <dir>` (default `./.forge`) precedes every
subcommand and names the project you are operating on.

Agents: call `nmt-forge status --json` first — it tells you which of these to
run next.


## `discover`

what does this language have? (reads the language card through the eval harness's resolver; absence = unknown, never zero)

**Arguments:**

- `code` — ISO 639-3 code (e.g. crk, fra, nav, arb)

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--cards-dir` — a directory of &lt;code>.json language cards (e.g. exported with `champollion network card <code> --json`). Default: $MT_EVAL_CARDS_DIR / $CHAMPOLLION_CARDS_DIR, a checkout or node_modules/champollion above the working directory, else the public card index (cached; reused offline)
- `--no-registry` — skip the mt-eval registry cross-check of eval datasets

## `init`

scaffold a project from a language card: workspace + starter config + NEXT_STEPS.md

**Arguments:**

- `code` — ISO 639-3 code of the TARGET language

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--dir` — project directory (default .)
- `--pair` — language pair: eng-crk, or 'eng>crk' (quote the > form — an unquoted > is a shell redirect) (default eng-&lt;code>)
- `--cards-dir` — a directory of &lt;code>.json language cards (see `discover --help`)
- `--model` (one of: byt5-small, byt5-small-lowmem, cpu-finetune, cpu-tiny, nllb-600m, auto) — model preset (default cpu-tiny; auto: byt5-small where there is a GPU forge can train on, else cpu-tiny, said why) — cpu-tiny: tiny transformer trained from scratch on your pairs — CPU, no download, minutes; weak by design, honest loop; cpu-finetune: fine-tune a small pretrained Marian/opus-mt model on CPU — ~300 MB download; usually stronger than cpu-tiny when a RELATED pair exists (you name the base); nllb-600m: NLLB-200 distilled 600M with LoRA — strongest start, needs a GPU (~2.5 GB download); byt5-small: Google's ByT5-small (300M parameters, reads bytes — no vocabulary to fit) fine-tuned on your pairs — ~1.2 GB download; Apple silicon or a GPU makes it hours, not days; byt5-small-lowmem: Google's ByT5-small (300M parameters, reads bytes — no vocabulary to fit) fine-tuned on your pairs — ~1.2 GB download; Apple silicon or a GPU makes it hours, not days — set up for a computer with 8–15 GB of memory (less memory per step, more time)
- `--no-card` — scaffold a language the card index doesn't have yet (everything a card would say is then unknown)
- `--name` — the language's name (with --no-card)
- `--base` — pretrained model for --model cpu-finetune (a Hugging Face id or a local dir, e.g. an opus-mt model for a RELATED pair); optional override for nllb-600m

## `preflight`

will &lt;command> refuse? every gate it will hit, with fixes (exit 2 if any gate fails)

**Arguments:**

- `target` — command to preflight: run|evaluate|export|serve|score|split|prereg|leak-audit

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--config` — run config for run/evaluate/export (default ./config.json) — checks it parses, its dev set, its data files, and that the backend's extra is installed

## `lint`

diagnose a battery manifest: weak registers → likeliest cause → the lever to pull next; every caveat mt-eval wrote on the same read's TestReport (a near-constant output, length, copies) is a finding, beside the headline chrF++ and its CI

**Arguments:**

- `manifest` — battery manifest json (guard: ci-scoring/battery); an export's is `<export>/evaluation/battery-hyps-battery.json`. A run's run-manifest.json lints the battery of every scored export of that run (refused, with the export command, when it has none)

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--run-manifest` — run manifest for schedule/transfer-plateau signals

## `split`

group-disjoint train/dev/test carve

**Arguments:**

- `corpus` — 

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--test` *(required)* — test rows to carve (≥ 0). Use 0 when your test set is a SEPARATE file (teacher-checked, private): register it with `registry add <name> <file> --role test` and carve only train/dev
- `--dev` — dev rows to carve (checkpoint selection runs on these; training refuses without a dev set)
- `--seed` *(required)* — 
- `--out` *(required)* — 
- `--source-field` — 
- `--target-field` — 
- `--register` — also register PREFIX-test / PREFIX-dev in the workspace
- `--allow-rotate` — with --register: replace PREFIX-dev / PREFIX-test when they are already registered with other content (e.g. re-splitting after leak-audit --clean-to). The rotation is ledgered with what it replaced and how often that content was read; without the flag a conflicting split is refused before any file is written
- `--near-dupe` — also keep NEAR-duplicates on one side (e.g. 0.6): rows whose source or target words overlap at ≥ this Jaccard are grouped, so sentences built on the same template/frame never straddle train and test. Use it when the split reports test rows with a near-twin in training. Templates can chain into one huge group on a small templated corpus: when a side would get far more rows than asked (over 1.5x), split refuses and says what to do
- `--max-group` — with --near-dupe: cap near-duplicate share-groups at N rows (strongest links first), so templates that chain cannot form one giant group. Exact-duplicate groups are never capped. Near-duplicate links left uncut are counted, and the split's near-twin check reports the twins that cross sides

## `leak-audit`

screen a corpus vs registered evals — explains what it would drop (exact / near-duplicate answers) and what it keeps on purpose (template siblings; a NEAR-duplicate prompt with a different answer — an IDENTICAL prompt is dropped), with examples; deterministic. With a fixed test set, --drop-test-twins also drops the training rows that are near-twins of it

**Arguments:**

- `corpus` — 

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--strict` — hard-fail on test/sealed hits
- `--clean-to` — write surviving rows here (plus an audit manifest next to it)
- `--drop-test-twins` — with --clean-to: ALSO drop the training rows that are near-twins of a registered test/sealed row (identical, or a word overlap — Jaccard — ≥ 0.6 on the source or the target side: the measure the test-score near-twin check uses), template siblings included. For a FIXED test set (teacher-written, registered — not carved by split, so split --near-dupe cannot help) whose rows mostly have a twin in training: without this, the test score measures recall of training phrases. Says how many rows it drops and what the strict subset becomes; refuses to leave nothing to train on. Also writes the twin-free model's config (--companion-config) and names the command that trains it
- `--companion-config` — with --drop-test-twins: where to write the config of the twin-free model (default: config-notwins.json beside the project's config.json) — the same config with its own run_name, data.gold and eval.near_dupe_corpus set to the --clean-to file. An existing file is never overwritten
- `--manifest` — content-free audit manifest path (default with --clean-to: &lt;clean-to>.audit.json)
- `--overwrite` — let --clean-to replace a file that is in use: one a project config trains on (data.gold, a synthetic lane, eval.near_dupe_corpus), one a run trained on, the corpus a registered split was carved from, or the output of a different audit (the all-data clean corpus vs the twin-free one). Refused without it
- `--full-indices` — --json: print every row-index list in full (by default each list longer than 5 shows its count and first 5; the audit file written beside --clean-to always keeps them in full)
- `--target-field` — 
- `--no-examples` — don't quote corpus rows in the human output
- `--show-text` — print corpus sentences even when the corpus (or the eval set a row matched) is local-only, sealed or consent-required — otherwise line numbers, ids and scores are printed instead. Only for a person at the terminal: an AI agent that reads this output sends it to its model provider. --json output never carries sentences

## `run`

single-command reproducible training run

**Arguments:**

- `config` — 

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--resume` — after a power cut, a crash or a stop: start again from the interrupted run's last checkpoint (its weights; a fresh optimizer; the epochs it had left) — a new run that says where it resumed from
- `--skip-disk-check` — start even when the disk check says the run will not fit (the estimate can be wrong); recorded in the run's manifest
- `--detach` — run as a bounded background job with a stall watchdog (returns at once; `nmt-forge jobs` / `status` show progress)
- `--job-name` — with --detach: the job's name
- `--stall-minutes` — with --detach: stop the job after this long with no progress (default 10, or 30x the median step time if longer)
- `--startup-minutes` — with --detach: stop the job if it shows no sign of life this long after starting (default 15)
- `--deadline-hours` — with --detach: hard limit (default: the config's time_budget_hours + 25%, else 24)
- `--show-text` — show corpus sentences inside error messages (e.g. a metric plugin's error quoting a row) even for local-only, sealed or consent-required corpora — otherwise they read [sentence withheld]. This command prints no sentences otherwise. Only for a person at the terminal: an AI agent that reads this output sends it to its model provider

## `evaluate`

close the loop: decode the config's battery with the run's SELECTED checkpoint, score it (CIs, prereg-gated) and auto-diagnose — no manual decode

**Arguments:**

- `run_manifest` — run-manifest.json written by `nmt-forge run`

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--config` — run-config path (defaults to the config embedded in the run manifest); must carry an eval block
- `--out-hyps` — where to write decoded battery hypotheses (default: alongside the run manifest)
- `--harness-out` — also write an mt-eval RunLog + TestReport here (built by the harness from this same read; they contain the eval set's text)
- `--glossary` — an evaluation glossary for the mt-eval report's terminology metric: JSON {"source term": "translation" or ["accepted", "forms"]} (or a coaching file's "dictionary") — what `mt-eval run --glossary` takes. A scoring input only: the model never sees it. Overrides the config's eval.glossary
- `--prereg` — the preregistration this run is judged against (an id from `nmt-forge status`). Needed when several preregs bind the test set for this run (e.g. two models on one fixed test set): forge refuses to guess. Without it: the only valid prereg, else the one this run's first test read was bound to, else the one pinned to this run's config hash
- `--show-text` — show corpus sentences inside error messages (e.g. a metric plugin's error quoting a row) even for local-only, sealed or consent-required corpora — otherwise they read [sentence withheld]. This command prints no sentences otherwise. Only for a person at the terminal: an AI agent that reads this output sends it to its model provider

## `export`

evaluate the run on its test battery (prereg-gated) AND package it: model/ (in the --out directory) is the deployable model — weights, tokenizer, forge-model.json, DEPLOY.md, champollion plugin manifest, no test sentences; evaluation/ beside it holds the battery report and the mt-eval RunLog + TestReport — your test sentences, never deployed

**Arguments:**

- `run_manifest` — run-manifest.json written by `nmt-forge run`

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--out` *(required)* — export directory (new/empty); gets model/ and evaluation/
- `--config` — run-config path (defaults to the embedded config)
- `--no-eval` — package without scoring the test battery (e.g. a sealed set already spent)
- `--no-model` — write the evaluation + mt-eval report only
- `--glossary` — an evaluation glossary for the mt-eval report's terminology metric: JSON {"source term": "translation" or ["accepted", "forms"]} (or a coaching file's "dictionary") — what `mt-eval run --glossary` takes. A scoring input only: the model never sees it. Overrides the config's eval.glossary
- `--endpoint` — URL the champollion plugin manifest points at (default `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/translate`)
- `--port` — 
- `--name` — plugin/model name (kebab-case; default nmt-forge-&lt;run>)
- `--force` — replace a non-empty --out directory
- `--prereg` — the preregistration this run is judged against (an id from `nmt-forge status`). Needed when several preregs bind the test set for this run (e.g. two models on one fixed test set): forge refuses to guess. Without it: the only valid prereg, else the one this run's first test read was bound to, else the one pinned to this run's config hash
- `--show-text` — show corpus sentences inside error messages (e.g. a metric plugin's error quoting a row) even for local-only, sealed or consent-required corpora — otherwise they read [sentence withheld]. This command prints no sentences otherwise. Only for a person at the terminal: an AI agent that reads this output sends it to its model provider

## `serve`

serve an exported model: champollion api contract (POST /translate) + OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions; binds 127.0.0.1

**Arguments:**

- `export_dir` — the model directory `nmt-forge export` wrote (model/ in its --out directory), or the export directory itself

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--host` — bind address (non-loopback requires a token)
- `--port` — port to listen on (default $NMT_FORGE_SERVE_PORT, else 8378); if it is in use, pick another and point the champollion endpoint at it
- `--token` — bearer token clients must send (default $NMT_FORGE_SERVE_TOKEN; required off-loopback)
- `--device` (one of: auto, cpu) — 
- `--no-hook` — serve WITHOUT the run's decode hook (reported on /health and every response)
- `--allow-locale` — also accept this locale code (repeatable) — e.g. --allow-locale en:crk when the export could not resolve the card aliases offline
- `--choose` — also record this export as the USER's deployment choice (as `nmt-forge choose` does). Without it a serve is recorded as served — a trial — never as the choice
- `--holders-agreed-by` — for a model whose output is local-only, served off-loopback: who among the data's holders agreed that what it writes may leave this machine (reported on /health)
- `--detach` — serve as a background job: returns once /health answers (stopped and written down if it does not within 2 min); `nmt-forge jobs stop <name>` stops it
- `--job-name` — with --detach: the job's name

## `choose`

record the user's deployment choice among several exports — the one `nmt-forge status` then names. Serving a model never records it

**Arguments:**

- `model_dir` — the chosen export's model directory (model/ in its --out directory)

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--note` — why (kept in the ledger), e.g. 'chosen by the clinical lead, 2026-10-04'

## `use-model`

switch config.json to a model preset (written out in full, recorded in the ledger) — the answer to the improve loop's offer of a stronger model

**Arguments:**

- `preset` — 

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--config` — 
- `--base` — the pretrained model, for a preset that needs one (cpu-finetune)
- `--answer` *(required)* (one of: yes, not-now) — the people's answer to the offer: not-now records it and changes nothing

## `monitor`

attach the human-facing GUI to a running (or finished) run dir: loss curves + floor + a loud stop button; read-only otherwise (new runs open it automatically)

**Arguments:**

- `run_dir` — the run directory under &lt;ws>/runs/

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--pid` — training process id — lets the stop button actually kill an attached run
- `--log` — the trainer's stdout log — makes the panel live from minute one (loss every logging step + rate/ETA) instead of waiting for the first checkpoint dump
- `--port` — 
- `--no-browser` —
